question: Pri každej poriadnej chate je pod strechou naukladané drevo, ktoré sa suší aj rok či dva. Akú časť hmotnosti čerstvo vyrúbaného dreva tvorí voda?
source_excerpt: Wood Species - Moisture Content and Weight

extra.why_interesting: A log looks and feels like solid, dry material, so players guess a small share such as a tenth. The answer is roughly half, which explains the woodpile stacked under the eaves of every chata and why you never burn freshly chopped wood in the stove.
extra.verification_notes: Green wood is typically ~45-60% water by fresh weight (about 100% dry-basis), so 'about half' is the best option; I derived this from the dry-to-wet-basis conversion rather than a directly quoted wet-basis figure (https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/amp/weigt-wood-d_821.html).

explanation: Čerstvé drevo je zhruba z polovice voda, takže v kachliach by sa teplo míňalo hlavne na jej odparovanie. Preto sa kúri až vysušeným drevom, ktoré viac hreje a menej dymí.

question: Zápalky na zakúrenie v piecke má na chate každý. Bezpečnostná zápalka sa však zapáli len o bok škatuľky. Ktorý chemický prvok je totiž na škrtadle, a nie na hlavičke?
source_excerpt: The striking surface contains red phosphorus; the match head is 45–55% potassium chlorate, with a little sulfur and starch.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone at the chata lights the stove with matches. Most people assume the match head holds everything needed to burn. In fact the key ingredient sits on the side of the box. A player who remembers that 'matches have phosphorus' can reason their way to the answer.
extra.verification_notes: Safety match striking surface contains red phosphorus while the head holds potassium chlorate and sulfur, per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safety_match

explanation: Na škrtadle je červený fosfor a na hlavičke chlorečnan draselný. Oheň vznikne až vtedy, keď sa pri škrtnutí stretnú, a preto zápalka o stenu ani o nohavice nechytí.
